'''Miklos Porkolab '''(born March 24, 1939) is a Hungarian-American [[physicist]] specializing in [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11603014.html|title=Porkolab, Miklos|website=history.aip.org|access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
In 1957, Porkolab emigrated from [[Hungary]] to [[Canada]]. He obtained his bachelor's degree at the [[University of British Columbia]] in 1963 and then his master's degree and Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 1964 and 1967 respectively. 

He moved to the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]], where he worked as a senior research physicist until 1975. During the following year, Porkolab worked at the [[Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics]] in Garching, Germany, under the auspices of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Foundation]] as a winner of the "US Senior Scientist Award". In 1977, he became professor of physics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he later led the Plasma Science and Fusion Center (PSFC) for many years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://web.mit.edu/physics/people/faculty/porkolab_miklos.html |title= Prof. Porkolab's biography on the APS website|publisher=APS|accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref>

Between 1991 and 2001, Porkolab served as editor of ''[[Physics Letters A]]'', in the Plasma Physics and Fluid Dynamics subsection. He also represented the U.S. Plasma Physics community for six years on the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] (IUPAP) Commission–16 (Plasma Physics) (1991-1997). Between 1992 and 1995, he served as a member of the National Research Council Subpanel on Plasma Science. In 1999, he served as chair of the Plasma Physics Division of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://physics.mit.edu/faculty/miklos-porkolab/|title=Porkolab's home page on the MIT website|publisher=MIT|accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref>

== Scientific contributions==
Whilst at Princeton, Porkolab concentrated on dispersive properties of [[Waves in plasmas|plasma waves]] and [[Plasma stability|instabilities]] in magnetized plasmas. Measurements corroborating the validity of the collisionless [[Boltzmann equation]] and demonstrating nonlinear scattering of [[Bernstein waves]] with wavelengths comparable to the electron [[Gyroradius|Larmor radius]] were obtained. Porkolab's work provided experimental verifications of [[Landau damping]], nonlinear resonant wave-wave scattering and parametric instabilities, also predicting upper hybrid solitons. 

From 1977, whilst at the MIT Physics Department, Porkolab joined the newly established [[MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center]], where he began experiments on lower hybrid current drive in [[tokamak]] plasmas. He also carried out investigations on ion cyclotron heating and mode conversion processes in multi-ion species fusion plasmas. [[Phase-contrast imaging]] (PCI) was developed by Porkolab's group both for use at the [[Alcator C-Mod]] tokamak and the [[DIII-D]] tokamak of [[General Atomics]] in [[San Diego]]. In recent years, PCI measurements contributed to the advanced in understanding of turbulence and [[Alfvén wave]] phenomena.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.apsdpp.org/publications/chronicles/DPP%202009%20Chronicle.pdf |title=Work by Prof. Porkolab in the APS Chronicle |publisher=APS |accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
For his work on radio frequency heating and noninductive current drive on the Versator II, the Alcator C and C-Mod tokamaks, Professor Porkolab shared the 1984 American Physical Society Excellence in Plasma Research Award (now the [[John Dawson Award]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/awards/dawson.cfm |title= John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research |publisher=Fusion Power Associates|accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref>

In 2009, Porkolab was awarded the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] by the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=Miklos%20Porkolab&year=2009 |title=Maxwell Prize awarded to Porkolab |publisher=APS |accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref> for<blockquote>''"pioneering investigations of linear and nonlinear plasma waves and wave-particle interactions; fundamental contributions to the development of plasma heating, current drive and diagnostics; and leadership in promoting plasma science education and domestic and international collaborations."''</blockquote>In 2013, he received the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] of the [[European Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite journal|title= Hannes Alfvén Prize 2013 |publisher=European Physical Society |doi= 10.1088/0741-3335/55/12/120301 |s2cid=250875759 |doi-access= }}</ref> for <blockquote>''"for pioneering investigations of linear and nonlinear plasma waves and wave-particle interactions; fundamental contributions to the development of plasma heating, current drive and diagnostics; and leadership in promoting plasma science education and domestic and international collaborations."''</blockquote>Porkolab was also awarded the Karoly Simony Memorial Plaque and Prize by the Hungarian Nuclear Society in 2007<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Hungarian+Nuclear+Society+honors+Miklos+Porkolab.-a0173375549 |title= Simony Medal awarded to Prof. Porkolab|publisher=MIT|accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref> and a Fusion Power Associates Distinguished Career Award in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://aries.pppl.gov/FPA/ARC10/fpn10-38.shtml |title= Porkolab, Ryutov to Receive Distinguished Career Awards |publisher=Fusion Power Associates|accessdate=3 October 2016}}</ref>

In 2016, Porkolab was elected an External Member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.mit.edu/2016/porkolab-honored-hungarian-academy-sciences-0523|title=Porkolab honored by Hungarian Academy of Sciences|website=MIT News|date=23 May 2016 |access-date=2020-02-17}}</ref>
